batch_note: Yes, two templates predict the key. (1) Seven of twelve textual items (A-01, A-03, B-01, B-02, C-01, C-03, D-01) use one option cast: a restatement of the pattern the passage says both accounts fit, its reversal, and a reversed pair over the passage's final contrast; the key is always the reversed-pair member that matches the hypothesis on the final sentence, so a test-wise student strikes two options on sight and decides the rest from one sentence. These are medium, not hard. The other five textual items (A-02, B-03, C-02, D-02, D-03) break the template and are the real hard-route items. (2) Six of twelve table items (A-04, A-06, C-04, C-05, D-05, D-06) state an 'every/any member of group X' claim; the key is always the strongest competitor inside X, and one option always names a non-X row that falls on the label column. The rule still needs arithmetic on A-04, A-06 and D-06, less so on C-04, C-05 and D-05. A-05 and B-05 are easy because only one option crosses the relevant group label. Weak minor signal: three of the four 'weaken' items are keyed A (A-02, C-02, D-02). Key letters overall A5/B6/C8/D5, no letter tell. All 24 keys agree with my cold phase-1 answers.
